title: Recover the shared TR-6S/TR-8S firmware key (64-bit block cipher) via NOR bootloader dump
description:
The TR-6S and TR-8S App1_Main images are ECB-encrypted under a SHARED 64-bit block-cipher key (proven: 66,233 identical ciphertext blocks across the two images). Recovering the key once decrypts BOTH product lines. The key + decrypt routine live in the bootloader in NOR flash (Infineon S29GL512S on TR-6S), not in any shipped update file.

Because the key is shared, the hardware dump can target EITHER a TR-6S or a TR-8S -- whichever is easier to access. Steps: (1) locate JTAG/SWD/UART debug pads or the parallel-NOR bus; (2) dump the NOR; (3) find the bootloader's decrypt routine, identify the cipher (DES/3DES/Blowfish/XTEA/CAST/custom Feistel) and extract the key; (4) validate by decrypting App1_Main and checking the 0x50 header checksum over the plaintext.

Leverage: any plaintext from one unit is a known-plaintext oracle for the 66k shared blocks of the other. Gated behind hardware access (phase gate: read-only until recovery/DFU path confirmed).

title: Reverse-engineer T-8 App_Panel (plaintext ARM) to learn Roland conventions
description: T-8 App_Panel is plaintext ARM Cortex-M, already imported to the Ghidra project (DD010_pnl_ARM.bin, base 0x08000000, 196 functions). Free desk work, no hardware. Goals: (1) identify the header CHECKSUM routine -- the 0x50 field appears in every image's header; if the panel image validates its own body with a known algorithm we may crack the checksum used across the encrypted images too. (2) Map peripheral usage (which STM32 peripherals, matrix scan for the 74HC138) to confirm the exact STM32G0 variant and pin map. (3) Establish Roland's compiler/toolchain fingerprint (libc stub, SystemInit) for cross-referencing the eventual decrypted E4E code. Related: cowbell-hu6.
notes: CHECKSUM RESOLVED (computationally, via known-plaintext — no ARM reversing needed). The header checksum (0x50 for App1_Main, 0x2c for compact App* layout) is STANDARD CRC-32 (zlib crc32, poly 0x04C11DB7, reflected, init/xorout 0xFFFFFFFF) over the image body. Proven: CRC-32 of the plaintext App_Panel body == its 0x53c790fb field exactly. Also proven the CRC is over PLAINTEXT: CRC-32 over the ciphertext of the encrypted images matches nothing (TR-6S 0x25f6cee3 != 0x46de65b3). => bootloader decrypts THEN CRCs. Bonus: this is a decryption ORACLE for cowbell-8o5 — correct key is the one whose decrypted-body CRC-32 == header field.

title: Characterize E4E via AIRA Compact Beat 8 reference platform
description:
The TR-6S main audio SoC is (candidate) a Roland E4E. The AIRA Compact 'Beat 8' shares a CONFIRMED Roland E4E (BGA, marked 'Roland E4E', lot 5100069694, date 2304) and is cheap, openable, firmware-downloadable, and already open on the bench. Use it as the reference platform to crack the E4E without a TR-6S teardown.

Context confirmed from board photos (2026-08-07):
- Beat 8 audio SoC = Roland E4E (discrete silicon, not marketing).
- Beat 8 panel MCU = ST STM32G0 (ARM Cortex-M0+, LQFP48) + 74HC138 matrix decoder.
- 8-pin SOIC marked 251/P2368 sits beside the E4E -- candidate external SPI NOR/EEPROM.
- App1_Main image load addr = 0x60000000 (ARM external-NOR-bank base) -> ARM ISA hypothesis for E4E.

Sub-tasks:
1. Download Roland's Beat 8 / AIRA Compact firmware update(s). Run through fw-extract/fw-analyze: is the container the same tar+App-header format? Is the payload ECB-encrypted like the TR-6S, or plaintext? Same 64-bit block cipher? Does the checksum algorithm reveal itself on a plaintext image?
2. Identify the 251/P2368 SOIC-8 (match marking to a datasheet). If SPI NOR: in-circuit SOIC-8 clip dump (CH341A/flashrom, no soldering) -> first look at real E4E-adjacent code/data.
3. If plaintext E4E code is obtained, confirm ISA (ARM vs other) and pick the Ghidra language spec. This retro-answers the TR-6S ISA question IF the two units share the E4E.

Acceptance: either (a) a decrypted/plaintext code region attributable to the E4E, or (b) a definitive ISA identification, whichever comes first. Feeds docs/hardware.md and architecture-questions.md.

Blocks: any TR-6S bootloader/decryption work. Cheaper and faster than the S29GL512S chip-off on the TR-6S.
notes:
CORRECTION: the Beat 8 board photos are third-party (Reddit), NOT the maintainer's hardware. We do NOT have a Beat 8 on hand. Split this bead by cost: (1) FREE/NOW = download Roland Beat 8 / AIRA Compact firmware and analyze container+encryption vs TR-6S (no hardware needed); (2) BLOCKED-ON-PURCHASE = the SOIC-8 clip-dump and any board probing require acquiring a unit first. The E4E-is-real-silicon and STM32G0 findings still stand as external corroboration.
FIRMWARE COMPARISON DONE (free half). Analyzed T8_UPD.BIN (T-8/Beat 8 v1.02) + TR8S_UP.bin (TR-8S v3.00) alongside TR6S. Results: (1) Container = same Roland tar+App-header format across all 3. (2) T-8 App_Main encrypted with a DIFFERENT key (0 shared blocks) -> NOT a key shortcut. (3) T-8 App_Panel is PLAINTEXT ARM Cortex-M -> imported to Ghidra, 196 functions, confirms panel-MCU ISA. (4) BONUS: TR-6S and TR-8S SHARE the encryption key (66,233 identical ciphertext blocks). The remaining hardware sub-task (SPI dump of E4E-adjacent flash) still needs a purchased unit and is lower priority now that ISA is confirmed via the panel image.

title: fw-extract: recognise and unwrap tar update containers
description:
TR6S_UP.bin (Roland TR-6S sys v2.00) is a GNU tar archive, not a raw firmware image — 'fw-extract identify' currently only knows exe/msi/dmg/pkg containers and misses it entirely. The archive holds two members under ./_tmp/: dd001_m0c0a_up.bin (2529328 B, encrypted App1_Main image) and dd001_init_param.bin (1376256 B, plaintext INIT param blob).

Scope:
- identify: detect tar (GNU/ustar magic 'ustar' at offset 0x101, plus the header-name/checksum sanity check) and report it as a container type.
- unpack: extract tar members natively (or shell to 'tar' consistent with the existing 7z/msiextract/xar delegation pattern), stripping the ./_tmp/ prefix.
- carve: rank the extracted members. Should surface dd001_m0c0a_up.bin as the dense/encrypted payload (entropy ~7.98) and flag dd001_init_param.bin as lower-entropy data.

Acceptance:
- 'fw-extract identify TR6S_UP.bin' prints tar (not 'unknown').
- 'fw-extract unpack' yields both members on disk.
- unit test with a small synthetic tar fixture (no Roland bytes committed).

Ref: docs/firmware-format.md 'Container — RESOLVED' section.
